content: 1. The enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of many drugs. Co-administration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated because it can lead to increased levels or effects of flibanserin, potentially causing severe hypotension or syncope. Close monitoring is required. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of adverse effects. 3. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 4. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of darunavir. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of flunisolide (inhaled) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Co-administration of SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone with darunavir or cobicistat may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect. Start with the lowest feasible dose and monitor the antidepressant response closely. 9. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of flurazepam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Alternatives should be considered if available. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Serious consideration should be given to using an alternative drug. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the severity of flutamide toxicities. 12. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of flutamide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone, leading to potential adverse effects. Monitor closely for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type symptoms. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluticasone (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone (inhaled) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type symptoms. 19. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone (intranasal) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 21. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 22. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with darunavir, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 23. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of cobicistat through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Carefully titrate the dose of antidepressants to the desired effect when co-administered with SSRIs and cobicistat. Start with the lowest feasible dose and monitor the response. 25. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 28. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Serious consideration should be given to using an alternative drug. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Serious consideration should be given to using an alternative drug. 31. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 33. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406, the major active metabolite of fostamatinib. Monitor for toxicities that may require dose reduction. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Co-administration of futibatinib with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the incidence or severity of futibatinib toxicities. 37. Garlic decreases the levels of darunavir through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of gefitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of gefitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 40. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Monitor closely. 41. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of gepirone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 43. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Consider alternatives to strong CYP3A4 inhibitors when co-administered with gilteritinib. If unavoidable, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. 46. Interrupt and reduce gilteritinib dosage in patients with serious or life-threatening toxicity. 47. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Consider alternative therapies that are not strong CYP3A inhibitors or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 50. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Serious consideration should be given to using an alternative drug. 51. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by decreasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Avoid co-administration of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with darunavir, a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 53. Darunavir decreases the effects of glimepiride through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance have been associated with protease inhibitors. Monitor closely. 55. Darunavir may increase or decrease the levels of glipizide. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider alternatives if available. 56. Darunavir decreases the effects of glyburide through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Green tea and darunavir may increase the risk of bleeding. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 61. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dosage to half of the recommended dose if co-administered. 62. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 63. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 66. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 67. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 68. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of darunavir. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 71. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 72. Avoid concomitant use of ibrutinib and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 73. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 74. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 75. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 76. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 77. If co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and follow recommendations for dosage modifications if adverse reactions occur. 78. Cobicistat decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 79. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 80. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone increases the levels of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 81. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Monitor closely. 82. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 83. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of imatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 84. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 85. Co-administration of SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone with darunavir or cobicistat may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect. Start with the lowest feasible dose and monitor the antidepressant response closely. 86. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of imipramine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 87. Carefully titrate the dose of antidepressants to the desired effect when co-administered with TCAs and cobicistat. Start with the lowest feasible dose and monitor the response.
